context: Quiz Tetris: a 60-second Tetris sprint. Clearing lines (and every 15 seconds without a question) pauses the falling pieces for one multiple-choice question; a right answer earns bonus points and slows the pieces down, a wrong one speeds them up, and the correct answer is shown either way. Write 6 to 8 questions so the player rarely sees one twice. `question` is a concise question (at most 90 characters). `options` are 2 to 4 short answers (1 to 4 words, at most 28 characters each), all distinct and plausible, with exactly one correct. `answer` is the index of the only correct option in `options` and must be smaller than the number of options. The game shuffles the options, so the correct option may be at any index. `context` is a short phrase naming the topic (at most 40 characters); it is shown to the player. Use only facts from the study material and prefer questions about different parts of it.
